blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
blocks.zh: 在动态场景中人机loco-management是非马尔科维语:提示随着物体的改变或隐藏而消失,或者随着机器人的转动和行走而离开视图,然而全身视觉语言动作(VLA)政策只看到现在. 我们呈现的是"全博迪Mem",一种以物体为导线的感知记忆,它保持了机器人在行动达到目标之前所看到的物体事件的史前记忆. SAM3跟踪任务对象,它们的事件在适应性预算范围内因果地选择了关键框架,动作专家通过交叉意念与对象符号编码外观,几何和时间一起阅读. 我们还贡献了HuMeGo,这是一个人文记忆基准,它有六个模拟和六个现实世界Unitree G1任务. 保持正确的帧而不是更多的帧,WatherBodyMem超越了无记忆和统一的模组基线,使其基础政策在模拟中的成功率从29.1%提高到72.6%,在真机器人上的成功率从36.7%提高到88.3%,同时也改进了标准SIMPLE任务(70.2%提高到86.9%).

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: Whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) models [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] , paired with learned whole-body controllers [ 4 , 5 ] , have advanced humanoid loco-manipulation considerably. Yet most of them act on the current observation alone, ignoring temporal dependencies, and thus fail in dynamic scenes where objects change state or are hidden [ 6 , 7 ] , moved or removed. Everyday cues are brief and seldom repeated: a guest waves from one of several identical tables while a waiter carries a tray, and when the waiter turns back, the hand is already down. Fig. 1 shows this situation on a real G1: a cola stops on two seats and a sprite on one, the robot turns away to fetch the cola, and when it comes back the seats look the same again, so a policy that sees only the current view cannot tell where the cola stopped first. Loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is thus non-Markovian: earlier events determine later decisions, which calls for memory. We refer to it as pre-history memory : the record of the object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. Such memory is especially hard for a humanoid, whose head camera moves as it turns and walks, so cues leave the view, and whose memory must be updated causally while whole-body control runs. Even dual-system designs [ 2 ] , in which a VLM planner acts as System 2, can reason over the history only if they locate the key frames. Existing memory strategies, mostly developed for tabletop arms, retain long frame histories [ 8 , 9 ] , which are costly and dilute brief cues; compress them [ 10 , 11 ] , losing detail; sample frames at fixed intervals [ 12 ] , missing brief cues; or select event frames tied to the robot’s own operations or learned from demonstrations [ 13 , 14 ] .
blocks.zh: 全体视觉-语言-动作(VLA)模型[1,2,3],与学习的全体控制器[4,5]对齐,已经大大推进了人性化的loco-操纵. 然而,它们中的大多数仅根据当前观测结果行事,忽略了时间依赖性,从而在物体变化状态或被隐藏[6,7],移动或移除的动态场景中失败. 每天的提示都很简短,很少重复:一个客人从几个相同的桌子上发出波浪,而一个服务员携带一个托盘,当服务员回头时,手已经下垂. 图1在真实的G1上显示了这种情况:一个可乐停在两个座位上,一个可乐停在一块宝石上,机器人转身去取可乐,当它回来时,座位再次看起来相同,因此只看到当前观点的政策无法先分辨可乐停在哪里. 动态场景中的洛科操纵因此是非马尔科文:较早的事件决定了以后的决定,这需要记忆. 我们把它称为史前记忆:机器人行动前所看到的物体事件记录。 这样的记忆对于人偶来说特别困难,它的头部相机在转动和行走时会移动,所以提示离开视野,在全身控制运行时,它的记忆必须因果更新. 即使是双系统设计[2],其中VLM计划员扮演System 2,只有当它们找到关键帧时,才能解释历史. 现有的内存战略大多是为平顶臂制定的,保留了长帧历史[8,9],这些历史成本昂贵,并稀释了短提示;压缩[10,11],丢失细节;样本帧固定间隔[12],缺失短提示;或者选择与机器人自身操作相连或从演示中学习的事件帧[13,14].

blocks.en: As humans remember the moments when the things they care about change rather than every moment [ 15 ] , we propose WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory for whole-body VLAs. First, a frozen SAM3 [ 16 ] , a promptable video segmentation model, tracks the task objects in the head-camera stream, and we detect when they appear, disappear, move or change shape, compensating for the camera’s own motion. Second, these object events causally select the key frames that fill an adaptive memory budget, stored as native backbone tokens along with mask-pooled object tokens. Finally, the action expert reads this memory via cross-attention and FiLM, so that whole-body actions depend on what happened, not only on what is visible.
blocks.zh: 当人类记得他们所关心的改变 而不是每一刻[15]的时候, 我们提议了WatherBodyMem, 一个全体VLA的物体引导感知记忆。 首先,一个冷冻的SAM3 [16],一个快速的视频分区模型,追踪头-相机流中的任务对象,我们探测到它们何时出现,消失,移动或改变形状,补偿相机自己的动作. 其次,这些对象事件因果地选择了填补适应性内存预算的密钥框架,与面具集合对象符号一起作为原生骨干符号存储. 最后,动作专家通过交叉注意和FiLM来读取这个记忆,这样整个身体的动作就取决于发生的事情,而不仅仅是可见的东西.

blocks.en: Existing humanoid benchmarks [ 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 ] keep the goal in view and do not test this problem, whereas memory benchmarks [ 12 , 21 ] are tabletop manipulation. We therefore introduce a memory-dependent humanoid loco-manipulation benchmark. Our contributions are as follows:

blocks.en: II-A Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation VLAs
blocks.zh: II-A 整体-Body 人文学科-管理VLA

blocks.en: Whole-body humanoid control uses learned whole-body controllers such as HOVER [ 22 ] , AMO [ 4 ] and SONIC [ 5 ] , and demonstrations are collected by whole-body teleoperation [ 23 ] . On top of such controllers, vision-language-action (VLA) policies map images and instructions to whole-body actions. Generalist VLAs such as π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} [ 24 ] generalize across scenes and are adapted to whole-body action spaces; GR00T [ 2 ] is an open foundation model for humanoids trained on real, synthetic and video data; Ψ 0 \Psi_{0} [ 1 ] pre-trains on human egocentric video and then fine-tunes on a smaller amount of real humanoid data; and WholeBodyVLA [ 3 ] learns a unified latent action space for loco-manipulation. These policies differ in their data, action spaces and controllers, but all of them condition on the current observation and a short proprioceptive history, so an event that has left the camera’s view can no longer affect their actions. Memory has so far been added mostly to robots that do not walk, e.g. EgoMI [ 25 ] keeps past views for a wheeled semi-humanoid with an actuated head and SOMA [ 26 ] builds a spatial memory from a movable head camera; to our knowledge, no prior work studies memory for whole-body loco-manipulation, where the robot’s own walking and turning move cues out of view. Concurrent work, POT-VLA [ 27 ] , keeps a 3D record of where each task object is now but not what happened before; WholeBodyMem keeps the past views in which objects changed.
blocks.zh: 全身人造物控制使用HOVER[22],AMO[4]和SONIC[5]等有学识的全身控制器,演示由全身远程操作收集[23]. 在这些控制器之外,视觉语言-动作(VLA)政策将图像和指令映射给全身行动. GR00T[2]是接受过真实,合成和视频数据训练的人类类的开放式基础模型; ^0\Psi_{0}[1] 预告人类自负的视频,然后对较少量的真人类数据进行微调; 以及 PartyBodyVLA[3] 学习一个统一的潜伏动作空间,用于loco操纵. 这些政策在数据,动作空间和控制器上各不相同,但所有这些政策都以目前的观测和短暂的自制历史为条件,因此离开镜头视野的事件不再会影响他们的行动. EgoMI[25] 保留了过去对一个轮式半人造头像的看法, SOMA[26] 从可移动的头像相机上建立空间记忆; 据我们所知, 整个身体的loco-操纵没有前期工作研究记忆, 机器人自己走出去, 同时期工作,POT-VLA [27],保留了每个任务对象现在在哪里的3D记录,但不是以前发生的情况;WholeBodyMem保留了对象改变的过去视图.

blocks.en: II-B Memory and Datasets for Robot Policies
blocks.zh: II-B 机器人政策记忆和数据集

blocks.en: Memory mechanisms. Memory for robot policies has been studied mainly on tabletop arms with fixed or wrist cameras [ 12 , 10 , 28 , 29 ] , and on mobile and navigation agents [ 30 ] . Long frame histories [ 9 , 8 ] grow in cost and dilute a short cue; compression into gist tokens [ 11 ] or memory banks and object slots [ 10 , 31 ] keeps the cost fixed but can lose the detail a decision needs; frame selection keeps native detail at a fixed budget, by uniform sampling [ 12 ] , retrieval [ 29 ] or events [ 13 , 14 ] . A humanoid adds two constraints: its own turning and walking move a cue out of the head camera’s view and change the viewpoint, and the memory must be updated causally while whole-body control runs. WholeBodyMem therefore selects frames by object events, measured relative to the scene after camera-motion removal, and reads them with action-query cross-attention and FiLM. Unlike SAM2Act+ [ 28 ] , which adopts SAM2’s memory mechanism, we use SAM3 only as a tracker whose object events select the past views the action expert reads. Datasets and benchmarks. Memory benchmarks are mostly tabletop [ 12 , 21 , 28 , 31 ] , and humanoid benchmarks [ 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 ] evaluate whole-body skills with the goal in view. Our benchmark fills this gap with whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation tasks whose decisions depend on a cue that is no longer in view.
blocks.zh: 记忆机制. 机器人政策的内存主要研究于有固定或腕相机的平顶臂[12,10,28,29],以及移动和导航代理[30]. 长帧历史[9,8] 成本增加,并稀释了短提示;压缩成吉祥符[11]或存储库和对象槽[10,31]保持成本固定,但可能失去决定需要的细节;帧选择通过统一抽样[12],检索[29]或事件[13,14],将本地细节保持在固定预算. 人造物会增加两个限制:它自己转身和走动会从头部相机的视线中移动一个提示,并改变观点,在全身控制运行时,内存必须因果更新. 因此,WatherBodyMem通过物体事件选择帧,在相机运动清除后相对于场景进行测量,并用动作-静态交叉注意和FiLM读取。 与采用SAM2 Act+ [28] 记忆机制的SAM2不同,我们只使用SAM3作为跟踪器,其物体事件选择了动作专家所读取的过去观点。 数据集和基准。 记忆基准大多为表盘[12,21,28,31],人文基准[17,18,19,20]结合目标评价全身技能. 我们的基准填补了这一空白,完成了全体人造机器人操纵任务,其决定取决于不再考虑的提示。

blocks.en: III-A Task Definition
blocks.zh: III-A 任务定义

blocks.en: We call a humanoid loco-manipulation task memory-dependent when, in a dynamic scene, the observation available at the decision does not determine the correct action. Each episode has three phases: in the cue phase, a scene change, such as a lamp that lights or a mug that is hidden, singles out one answer y y from a small set 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} (two or three pads); in the retention phase, the robot performs whole-body skills that are the same for every answer; and in the decision phase, from a time t d t_{d} on, a whole-body action must follow y y . A cue can become unobservable in two ways: it can end, as when a light goes off or an object is hidden ( scene-induced ), or it can leave the head camera’s view as the robot turns and walks ( motion-induced ). We require that (i) the change is no longer observable at t d t_{d} , whether scene-induced or motion-induced; (ii) neither the instruction nor the robot’s motion before t d t_{d} depends on y y ; and (iii) y y is balanced over 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} . A policy without memory then cannot infer y y from the current view (chance: 1 / | 𝒴 | 1/|\mathcal{Y}| ), so we score memory-decision accuracy separately from manipulation success (Sec. V-A ).
blocks.zh: 在动态场景中,当决定中可用的观察不能确定正确的动作时,我们称人性化的loco-manapulation任务依赖记忆. 每集分三个阶段:在提示阶段,场景变化,如灯光或杯子被隐藏,从一个小集Y\mathcal{Y}中挑出一个答案y(两个或三个垫);在保留阶段,机器人执行每个答案相同的全身技能;在决定阶段,从时间t d_{d}开始,全身动作必须跟随y. 一个提示可以通过两种方式变得不可观察:它可以结束,比如当一个灯光熄灭或者一个物体被隐藏(场景引发)时,或者它可以在机器人转动和行走时离开头镜头的视线(动作引发). 我们要求 (一) 变化在 t d t_{d} 不再被观察到, 无论是场景引起的还是运动引起的;(二) 指令或机器人在 t d_{d} 之前的动作都不取决于 y ;以及 (三) y y 与 Y\ mathcal{Y} 的平衡. 没有内存的政策则不能从当前视图中推断y(chance:1/| Y| 1/|\mathcal{Y}|),因此我们得分内存决定精度与操纵成功(sec. V-A.)分开.

blocks.en: The kind of change determines the memory a decision needs: what changed (object memory, O), where an object went (spatial, S), or when and how often it changed (temporal, T), as in the reference, permanence and counting tasks of RoboMME [ 12 ] . Our six simulated tasks (Fig. 2 ) cover all three. A lamp flashes one to three times in FlashPad (T); a mug disappears behind one of three screens while a decoy mug leaves in HideMug (S); a ball is concealed under one of three cups, which are then swapped, in ShellGame (S); one of two coloured lamps lights up in LitLamp (O); and one of three pads blinks for 0.2 s in BlinkPad and TouchPad (O). Afterwards, the robot puts the carried object on the indicated pad or, in TouchPad, touches that pad. Because the cues are short-lived or occluded [ 6 , 7 ] while the robot watches, these suites isolate scene-induced loss; the real-world tasks additionally introduce motion-induced loss (Sec. V-E ).
blocks.zh: 这种变化决定了一个决定需要的内存:什么变化(对象内存,O),一个对象去的地方(空间,S),或者何时和频率变化(时间,T),如RoboMME的参考文献,持久性和计数任务[12]. 我们的六个模拟任务(图2)涵盖了所有三个任务. 一盏灯在FlashPad(T)中闪了1至3次;一个杯子在三个屏幕后面消失,而一个诱饵杯子在HideMug(S)中离开;一个球被隐藏在三个杯子的下面,然后在ShellGame(S)中互换;一个彩色灯光在LitLamp(O)中闪烁;一个3个垫子在BlinkPad和TouchPad(O)中闪烁0.2 s. 之后,机器人将携带的物体放置在指示的垫上,或者在TouchPad中,触摸该垫. 因为提示是短寿命的或被占用的[6,7],而机器人手表,这些套房隔离场景引起的损失;现实世界的任务额外引入了运动引起的损失(Sec. V-E.).

blocks.en: III-B Data Generation
blocks.zh: 三-B 数据生成

blocks.en: A scripted whole-body expert generates the demonstrations in six steps. 1. Task specification. A script sets the single-table scene (the object to carry, the answer pads, the cue objects), the cue timeline and the skill sequence. A seed fixes the object pose ( ± \pm 3 cm, ± \pm 8 cm, ± \pm 0.15 rad), the robot’s spawn offset ( ± \pm 3 cm), the cue layout and the appearance; the answer is drawn independently. 2. Expert rollout. In MuJoCo (2 ms physics, 50 Hz control), the cue plays for a fixed, task-specific window. In FlashPad, HideMug, ShellGame and LitLamp it starts 0.5 s into the episode, while the robot still stands at the table before the grasp and lift; in BlinkPad it starts 0.5 s after the lift, and in TouchPad at a random time 1.9–3.7 s into the episode, before the robot turns. A precomputed Dex3 grasp, cuRobo arm planning and AMO [ 4 ] leg and waist balancing drive the robot through the skill sequence. 3. Selection. An episode is kept if the object stays held after the lift (in the five carrying tasks) and the cue is visible to the head camera during its window; kept episodes are balanced over the answers. 4. Rendering. Recorded states are replayed in Isaac Sim and rendered from the head camera ( 640 × 360 640{\times}360 , 50 Hz) with per-episode randomized background distractors, materials and lighting. 5. Export. Episodes are exported in the LeRobot v2.1 format ( 32-D state, 36-D whole-body action, 50 Hz video), each ending 1 s after the placement. 6. Training and test split. Each memory task has 100 training demonstrations and 90 test scenes from seeds distinct from training. Test seeds pass the same selection as the training episodes and stay in distribution: layout and expert rollout within the training range, table materials seen in training. They are balanced over the answers and the three randomization levels.

blocks.en: Task specification. A script sets the single-table scene (the object to carry, the answer pads, the cue objects), the cue timeline and the skill sequence. blocks.en: As shown in Table II , we contrast our benchmark with robot memory benchmarks and with humanoid imitation benchmarks collected on the same platform and control frequency (Unitree G1, 50 Hz). Two properties set it apart. Extended horizons: an average episode spans 1,155 control steps (23 s), compared with 818, 611 and 322 steps in HumanoidMimicGen, HumanoidArena and SIMPLE, respectively. Decisions that require memory: each task presents a short-lived cue that occupies only 0.8–14.7% of an episode and has to be remembered for 13.5–22.5 s after it disappears (task medians). Overall, 40.7% of the steps come after the decision point, where, following conditions (i) and (ii) in Sec. III-A , the vanished cue provides the sole evidence for the correct action. In contrast, no step of the humanoid benchmarks depends on a vanished cue, and the memory benchmarks use arms, not humanoids.

blocks.en: The memory is built in three stages (Fig. 3 , left): SAM3 tracks the task objects, object events flag the frames where they change, and a causal selector fills an adaptive budget.

blocks.en: Algorithm 1 Causal memory selection at time t t
blocks.zh: 算法 1 时间 t 的因子内存选择

blocks.en: Memory budget. A memory frame keeps the K = 77 K{=}77 native tokens ( 7 × 11 7{\times}11 grid) of the frozen vision tower, and the budget is B max = 7 B_{\max}{=}7 frames, the current and six past ones: 539 memory tokens plus at most 14 object tokens (Sec. IV-C ). Tokens are cached, so re-selecting a frame is free. Unlike a pooled summary, native tokens keep the small regions a decision may hinge on (a cue can cover under 1% of the image), but only six past frames fit, so which are kept matters.

blocks.en: Object tracking. The task decides what to remember: a frozen SAM3 [ 16 ] tracks the task objects over the episode so far ( o 0 : t o_{0:t} in Fig. 3 ), prompted with one or two short phrases (e.g. “blue cup” in ShellGame, “cracker box” in Handover, T3 in Table I ), and returns a mask, a box and a confidence per frame and object. Prompts are written once per task by Claude Opus 5.5 and fixed before evaluation; the event rules and thresholds below are shared by all tasks. In simulation, SAM3 tracks every 50-Hz control step, and frame counts below refer to tracked frames. A similarity transform fitted to background features of consecutive frames removes camera motion, so object motion is measured relative to the scene.
blocks.zh: 物体追踪。 任务决定了要记住什么:一个冰冻的SAM3[16]追踪了迄今为止该集中的任务对象(o 0:t o_{0:t}在图3中),用一个或两个短短语(如ShellGame中的"蓝色杯子",Handover中的"cracker box",表1中的T3)引发,并返回一个面具,一个盒子和每个帧和对象的自信. 提示由克劳德·奥普斯(Claude Opus 5.5)写出一次,并在评价前固定;以下的事件规则和阈值由所有任务共享. 在模拟中,SAM3跟踪每50赫兹控制步骤,下面的帧计数指的是跟踪帧. 与连续帧背景特征相适应的相似性变换消除了相机运动,因此相对于场景来测量物体运动.

blocks.en: Object events. A past frame becomes a memory candidate only if a tracked object in it appears, disappears (we keep its last visible frame), reappears, moves by over 3% of the image diagonal after camera-motion removal, or changes shape (mask overlap with the previous one below 65%). Events are ranked by type, disappearance and reappearance first, then by confidence; detections below 0.35 are ignored. For example, a blinking pad appears and a hidden mug disappears.
blocks.zh: 物体事件. 只有当一个跟踪对象出现,消失(我们保留其最后一个可见的帧),重新出现,在相机移动除去后移动超过图像对角的3%,或者改变形状(与前一个在65%以下重叠)时,过去的帧才会成为内存候选. 事件先按类型,失踪和重现排序,然后依信心排序;0.35以下的探测被忽略. 例如,一个闪烁的垫子出现,一个隐藏的杯子消失.

blocks.en: Causal selection. At each time t t (Algorithm 1 ), the first, middle and current frames are always kept, and up to four slots go to the top-scoring event frames, skipping one whose objects all have a selected frame within 5 frames. The remaining slots stay empty, so the memory holds 3 to 7 frames (5.4 on average); the variant without adaptive memory, used on SIMPLE, fills all seven. Only frames up to t t are eligible, so the memory never depends on later frames; seven evenly spaced frames form our Uniform memory control.
blocks.zh: 因缘选. 每次 t t (算法 1 ),总是保留第一,中和当前帧,最多有四个插槽到最高评分的事件帧,跳过一个其对象在5个帧内都有选定帧. 其余的空位保持空位,因此内存持有3到7帧(平均5.4);SIMPLE上使用的无适应性内存的变体填充了全部7帧. 只有高达 t t 的帧才有资格,因此内存从不依赖于后期帧;七个均匀的间距帧构成我们的统一内存控制.

blocks.en: Decision head. To map the remembered cue to a pad, a learned query attends over the memory and object tokens and a null token, and an MLP outputs one logit per answer, trained with a cross-entropy loss on the demonstrated answer from the decision step on. The softmax of these logits, the dynamic weights w w (Fig. 3 ), enters every block’s adaptive layer norm through a zero-initialized map on the time embedding, so training starts from the head-free policy.
blocks.zh: 决定头目. 要将记忆中的提示映射到一个垫上,一个学习过的查询会从内存和对象的符号和一个无效的符号上进行,一个 MLP 输出一个登录每个答案,经过训练,在从决定步骤上显示的答案上出现交叉内质损失. 这些logits的软马克,动态权重w(图3),通过嵌入时间上的零初始化地图进入每个区块的适应层规范,因此训练从免头政策开始.

blocks.en: V Experiments
blocks.zh: V 实验

blocks.en: Our experiments answer four questions: Q1 Does adding memory cost reactive skills on the 14 standard SIMPLE tasks, or even improve them? Q2 On our six memory tasks, does WholeBodyMem act on vanished cues that memoryless policies miss? Q3 What is the role of pre-history memory: does object guidance, not capacity, explain the gain, and what do key frames, object tokens, the decision head, adaptive memory and memory attention each contribute? Q4 Does memory carry over to a real Unitree G1, where the robot also turns away from the cue?
blocks.zh: 我们的实验回答了四个问题: 问题1 在14个标准SIMPLE任务中加入内存成本反应技能,甚至改进它们? 问题2 在我们的六项记忆任务上,WholeBodyMem是否在消失的提示上采取行动,即无记忆政策错过了? 问题3 历史前记忆的作用是什么:对象引导而非能力,解释收益,以及关键帧,对象符,决定头,适应性记忆和记忆关注每个贡献什么? 问题4 内存会转移到真正的Unitree G1上吗?

blocks.en: V-A Setup
blocks.zh: V-A 设置

blocks.en: Simulation. All simulated experiments use SIMPLE [ 18 ] with the robot, 36-D whole-body action and rendering of Sec. III-B . AMO [ 4 ] drives the lower body in the memory tasks and in the two SIMPLE motion-planning tasks (T2, T4), and SIMPLE’s decoupled whole-body controller drives it in the other 12 SIMPLE tasks, whose demonstrations are teleoperated. Each policy runs as a server that the unmodified SIMPLE evaluation client, which also runs our memory tasks, queries once per action chunk.
blocks.zh: 模拟. 所有模拟实验都使用SIMPLE [18] 与机器人,36-D全体动作和渲染Sec. III-B. AMO [4] 在内存任务和两个SIMPLE运动规划任务(T2,T4)中驱动下体,SIMPLE的脱钩全体控制器在其他12个SIMPLE任务中驱动,其演示是远程操作. 每个策略都作为服务器运行,未修改的SIMPLE评价客户端也运行我们的内存任务,每个动作块一次查询.

blocks.en: Real robot. We use a Unitree G1 (29 DoF) with Dex3 hands and a head-mounted RealSense D435 ( 640 × 360 640{\times}360 , 30 Hz). The policy runs on one RTX 5090 with real-time chunking [ 40 ] : of the H = 30 H{=}30 predicted actions, the first 24 are executed before the next chunk takes over; SONIC [ 5 ] executes its 64-D motion token and 14-D hand targets at 50 Hz, and SAM3 tracks one frame per executed chunk (every 24 frames, about 1.25 Hz).

blocks.en: Baselines. All baselines are trained by us on the same demonstrations. (i) Policies without memory : InternVLA-M1 [ 32 ] , Diffusion Policy [ 33 ] , ACT [ 34 ] , EgoVLA [ 35 ] , π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} [ 24 ] , GR00T [ 2 ] and Ψ 0 \Psi_{0} [ 1 ] , the memoryless base policy. (ii) Uniform memory (RoboMME-style): as no published memory method exists for whole-body humanoid VLAs, we adapt the best-performing memory of RoboMME [ 12 ] , evenly sampled frames read through a memory modulator (FrameSamp + Modul), to our tasks. It is the Uniform memory control of Sec. IV-B , i.e. WholeBodyMem with evenly spaced frames and no object tokens or decision head, at the same 539-token budget (512 in RoboMME), with native instead of pooled tokens, as a cue can cover under 1% of the image; in an earlier evaluation on T5, T6 and T8, RoboMME’s original 32 pooled frames of 16 tokens scored the same as this adaptation (both 53.3%). On the real robot, we compare with Ψ 0 \Psi_{0} (Sec. V-E ).

blocks.en: Evaluation. Every policy follows the standardized protocol of SIMPLE [ 18 ] at three randomization levels (L0: visual and distractor randomization; L1: plus lighting; L2: plus spatial perturbation). The 14 SIMPLE tasks, which need no cue memory, use 10 episodes per level; our six memory tasks use 30 episodes per level (balanced answers; Sec. III-B ). An episode succeeds if its final condition holds (e.g. the object lies on the correct pad). On the memory tasks we also report memory-decision accuracy , the fraction of episodes in which the decision head picks the cued answer, otherwise the fraction of placements or touches on the cued pad.
blocks.zh: 评价。 每个政策都遵循SIMPLE [18] 在三个随机化级别上的标准化协议(L0:视觉和分散式随机化;L1:+照明;L2:+空间扰动). 14个SIMPLE任务不需要提示内存,每关使用10集;我们的6个内存任务每关使用30集(均衡的答案;sec. III-B.). 一个插曲如果其最终条件保持(例如对象位于正确的垫子上)则成功. 关于内存任务,我们也报告内存决定的准确性,决定头选择提示答案的片段,否则在提示垫上放置或触碰的片段.

blocks.en: V-B Results on Standard Loco-Manipulation Tasks (Q1)
blocks.zh: V-B 标准 Loco 管理任务的结果(问题1)

blocks.en: Memory does not cost reactive skills. On the 14 SIMPLE tasks (Table I ), WholeBodyMem matches or exceeds the best baseline on every task and reaches 86.9% success, against 70.2% for Ψ 0 \Psi_{0} and 76.9% for Uniform memory. These tasks need no cue memory, but the moving head camera loses targets as the robot walks and bends, and one frame hides task progress; past frames fill these gaps, and object tokens locate objects more finely. Accordingly, the gain over Uniform memory is largest where the robot walks to or between its targets: T6 (21 vs. 13) and T8 (20 vs. 11) give 17 of the 42 extra successes, while both solve T2 and T9.
blocks.zh: 记忆不花费反应能力。 在14项SIMPLE任务(表一)中,WatherBodyMem匹配或超过每项任务的最佳基线,成功率达到86.9%,而0\Psi_{0}的为70.2%,统一记忆为76.9%。 这些任务不需要提示内存,但移动的头摄像头会随着机器人行走和弯曲而丢失目标,一个帧会隐藏任务进度;过去帧会填补这些空白,对象符会更精细地定位对象. 因此,在机器人走进或走进目标之间的情况下,超过统一记忆的收益最大:T6(21对13)和T8(20对11)给出了42项额外成功中的17项,同时解决T2和T9.

blocks.en: V-D Object-Guided vs. Uniform Memory (Q3)
blocks.zh: V-D 对象引导对统一内存(Q3)

blocks.en: Object guidance, not capacity, explains the gain. At Uniform memory’s budget (seven frames, 539 tokens), choosing frames by object events alone (WholeBodyMem w/o object tokens, which lacks the decision head) lifts success from 44.4% to 60.4% (Table IV ), and adaptive memory loses nothing with 22.9% fewer tokens: the role of pre-history memory is to keep the right frames, not more.
blocks.zh: 对象引导,而非容量,解释收益. 在统一记忆的预算(7帧,539个令牌)中,单凭对象事件选择帧(WholeBodyMem w/o对象令牌,缺乏决定头)将成功率从44.4%提升到60.4%(表四),适应记忆则以22.9%的减少的令牌失去一切:史前记忆的作用是保持正确的帧,而不是更多.

blocks.en: Every part contributes. Of the 28.2-point gain over Uniform memory, key frames give 16.0, object tokens 5.3, the decision head 4.7 and adaptive memory 2.2 (Table IV ): key frames keep brief cues that evenly spaced frames miss, object tokens identify which object changed, and the decision head maps the cue to a target pad, so its answer labels explain only about a sixth of the gain. Memory fed to the frozen VLM as context instead of through the memory attention falls below even the memoryless Ψ 0 \Psi_{0} .

blocks.en: VI Limitations and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六. 限制和结论

blocks.en: We studied the role of pre-history memory, the object events seen before the robot acts on its goal, in humanoid loco-manipulation, with WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory for whole-body VLAs, and a humanoid memory benchmark. Object events select the few past views that matter, which the action expert reads within an adaptive budget: keeping the right frames matters more than keeping more, so the policy acts on vanished cues in simulation and on a real G1 without losing reactive skills. SAM3 misses a cue whose object is never detected, online tracking adds inference cost, rendering leaves a sim-to-real gap, and the simulated demonstrations are scripted. Remembering before acting on the goal is a first step toward humanoids that act on what happened, not only on what is visible.
blocks.zh: 我们研究了史前记忆的作用,机器人行动前看到的物体事件,在人性化的loco-操纵中,用OverBodyMem,全体VLA的物体导感记忆,以及人性化记忆基准. 目标事件选择了少数过去重要的观点, 行动专家在适应性预算范围内读到这些观点: 保持正确的框架比保存更多的重要, 因此政策行为在模拟和真正的G1中消失的提示上, SAM3错过了从未检测到对象的提示,在线跟踪增加了推论成本,渲染留下了模拟到真实的缺口,模拟演示被脚本化. 在行动之前记住这个目标,是人类对所发生事情采取行动的第一步,而不仅仅是对可见事物采取行动。
